reviews.title: Only Useful on Some Aspects
reviews.text:
Unless you have Bunpo Platinum, you can’t really do much with this app except self-study. Platinum grants you access to practicing dialogue based on different levels and topics. I purchased just the Bunpo Lifetime where I have access to all languages and grammar lessons.  But there’s no conversation/dialogue practice unless you’re willing to upgrade.  Conversation, I believe, is far more important in everyday life to get by than passing a test.

Also, some of the grammar lessons can be explained simpler. They use rather heavy grammatical terms like “append” and “constituents.”  You can get used to it, but it makes some of the lessons unusually hard to understand because they’re written like that.  I happen to rely more on the examples than the explanations themselves.

reviews.title: Paywalls and weird formatting.
reviews.text:
I’ve been getting back into the grind of learning Japanese, so I decided to try this app. The first two courses were great, they were easy to understand, and if I made mistakes I could get an explanation on where I went wrong. However, the explanation feature suddenly got paywalled after a few courses. There was also a point where I was stuck on a lesson not because I got the material wrong, because I was formatting it incorrectly. I had to spend nearly 20  minutes just to figure out where I went wrong with my formatting because the explanation was paywalled and you have to pay $20 (USD) to have access to the explanation feature. That is a lot of money for me, and I wish more language learning apps would make learning more accessible for people who don’t have money to throw at a monthly subscription.  After just five lessons, you’re suddenly blocked from the sixth lesson without a subscription, you can skip that lesson, but you can’t do the 7th lesson which is a test that’s required to continue.

The app was also inaccessible to those who need larger screens. It was not adjusted so the keyboard was covering text that was important to read. (You cannot simply slide down the keyboard to read and then re-enable it. It senses any kind of tap or slide as an answer so you would be accidentally submitting something without answering it.) I personally do not have a huge vision impairment, I use the larger screen feature so that I don’t fat finger my keys. However, I’d imagine this sucks for people who DO need that built-in feature to make their phones more accessible.

Now that I mentioned that I would like to Segway onto the fact that there’s a bug that makes your keyboard stuck, and you cannot simply just slide down because it thinks you’re submitting your answer rather than adjusting your keyboard.

reviews.title: Good app, but requires a subscription
reviews.text: The app was initially very good to work with as a person who did not want to pay for premium. I was initially using Duolingo but I did not like how they taught Asian languages. However this app was very good to learn from. I went through lessons, took notes and learned a lot very fast. Until I was blocked by a paywall and unable to continue the beginner course. You can unlock a few other lessons without paying, but there is not much of a way you can continue because if you do it for free there will be a huge gap in the things you learn. I love the way this app teaches you, but it’s hard to choose it over other apps like Duolingo or Memrise when they are primarily free. It might be better if the lessons were free, but premium just had better things to help you learn, like the ai tutor or the ability to access leaderboards or things like that? Just so people who can’t pay can still learn a lot from the app
